{{Short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Tabachnikov Dmitry Fuchs.jpg|thumb|Tabachnikov (on the left) with Dmitry Fuchs in [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics|Oberwolfach]], 2006]]

'''Sergei Tabachnikov''', also spelled '''Serge''', (born in 1956) is an American mathematician who works in [[geometry]] and [[dynamical system]]s. He is currently a Professor of Mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].

== Biography ==
He earned his Ph.D. from [[Moscow State University]] in 1987 under the supervision of [[Dmitry Fuchs]] and [[Anatoly Fomenko]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://genealogy.impa.br/id.php?id=87623 |title=The Mathematics Genealogy Project - Serge Tabachnikov |access-date=2015-03-13 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402132540/http://genealogy.impa.br/id.php?id=87623 |archive-date=2015-04-02 }}</ref> He has been living and working in the USA since 1990.

From 2013 to 2015 Tabachnikov served as Deputy Director of the [[Institute for Computational and Experimental Research in Mathematics]] (ICERM) in [[Providence, Rhode Island]].<ref>https://icerm.brown.edu/about/include/icerm%20newsletter_summer%202015.pdf{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} ICERM Summer 2015 Newsletter</ref> He is now Emeritus Deputy Director of ICERM.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://icerm.brown.edu/people/#tab_emeritus |title=ICERM Emeritus Leadership |access-date=2025-08-20 |archive-date=2017-06-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170611015942/https://icerm.brown.edu/people/#tab_emeritus |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list-institution | title=American Mathematical Society}}</ref>  He has served as Editor-in-Chief of the journal ''[[Experimental Mathematics (journal)|Experimental Mathematics]]'', and is currently serving as Editor-in-Chief of the ''[[Arnold Mathematical Journal]]'' and as co-Editor-in-Chief of the ''[[Mathematical Intelligencer]]''.<ref>{{cite journal
| title=EOV Editorial Board
| journal=Experimental Mathematics
| date=2018
| volume=27
| issue=4
| pages=507
| doi=10.1080/10586458.2018.1500849 | doi-access=free
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/40598 |title=Arnold Mathematical Journal|date=2024 |publisher=SpringerLink}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/283 |title=Mathematical Intelligencer|date=2025 |publisher=SpringerLink}}</ref>

A paper on the [[variability hypothesis]] by [[Ted Hill (mathematician)|Theodore Hill]] and Tabachnikov was accepted and retracted by ''The Mathematical Intelligencer'' and later ''[[The New York Journal of Mathematics]]'' (''NYJM''). There was some controversy over the mathematical model, the peer-review process, and the lack of an official retraction notice from the ''NYJM''.<ref name="TheScientist">{{Cite web |url=https://www.the-scientist.com/news-opinion/a-twice-retracted-paper-on-sex-differences-ignites-debate-64873 |title=A Twice-Retracted Paper on Sex Differences Ignites Debate |last=Azvolinsky |first=Anna |date=2018-09-27 |website=[[The Scientist (magazine)|The Scientist]] |access-date=2018-11-03 }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
